chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Abī Ḥammād, from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Nawfalī, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Mukhtār, from a man, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Accursed, accursed is the one who worships the dīnār and the dirham. Accursed, accursed is the one whose sleeve is blind. Accursed, accursed is the one who has intercourse with an animal.”

key_terms.أَعْمَى: Blind; indicating blindness or severe lack of perception.
key_terms.الدِّرْهَمَ: The silver coin; here, money and worldly gain.
key_terms.الدِّينَارَ: The gold coin; here, wealth and material riches.
key_terms.عَبَدَ: Worshipped or devoted himself in a servile manner.
key_terms.مَلْعُونٌ: Accursed; one cast away from divine mercy.

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about worshipping wealth and other accursed acts?
ai.summary: This hadith condemns extreme moral corruption in emphatic terms. It censures devotion to wealth, points to a state of blindness and deprivation, and denounces intercourse with animals as a grave and accursed act. The report serves as a forceful ethical warning against spiritual and moral degradation.
